questions.article: From the Desk of the Editorial Director
questions.q: A British officer is said to have wired London, “Kindly advise how to kill a tiger nonviolently.” What does the editorial say Gandhi had done to cause such bafflement?
options: Moved the struggle from the battlefield to the moral realm, where force had no answer
Yes. Lasting change is won in the realm of ideas.
Raised a larger army
Not quite. The article says: Moved the struggle from the battlefield to the moral realm, where force had no answer.
Kept his plans secret
Not quite. The article says: Moved the struggle from the battlefield to the moral realm, where force had no answer.
Refused all contact with the British
Not quite. The article says: Moved the struggle from the battlefield to the moral realm, where force had no answer.
questions.rationale: “Gandhi had moved the fight from battlefield to the moral realm, where the empire had no weapon.”

questions.q: A shopkeeper in Kigali was asked why he spoke English when he could not speak it correctly. What did he reply?
options: “I speak incorrect English so that I may be able to speak correct English”
Right. Within two years he was fluent.
“English is not important”
Not quite. The article says: “I speak incorrect English so that I may be able to speak correct English”.
“I have no time to learn properly”
Not quite. The article says: “I speak incorrect English so that I may be able to speak correct English”.
“My customers do not mind”
Not quite. The article says: “I speak incorrect English so that I may be able to speak correct English”.
questions.rationale: “The shopkeeper simply replied, ‘I speak incorrect English so that I may be able to speak correct English.’”

questions.q: The article distinguishes willing from wishing. What does it advise?
options: Wish for as much as possible
Not quite. The article says: Follow a true, strong will – which unfolds hidden potential – not an unrealistic wish.
Follow a true, strong will – which unfolds hidden potential – not an unrealistic wish
Yes. A shock taken seriously can awaken the mind.
Wait for a favourable moment
Not quite. The article says: Follow a true, strong will – which unfolds hidden potential – not an unrealistic wish.
Avoid setting any goal
Not quite. The article says: Follow a true, strong will – which unfolds hidden potential – not an unrealistic wish.
questions.rationale: “There is a difference between willing and wishing. Do not follow any unrealistic wish: follow your true will.”

questions.q: Stars follow laws and animals follow instinct. What does the article reason from this about human beings?
options: Science can supply every answer
Not quite. The article says: It is unlikely that the one creature charged with moral choice was left without guidance – so revelation is reasonable to expect.
Humans should live by instinct too
Not quite. The article says: It is unlikely that the one creature charged with moral choice was left without guidance – so revelation is reasonable to expect.
It is unlikely that the one creature charged with moral choice was left without guidance – so revelation is reasonable to expect
Well reasoned. Provision elsewhere suggests provision here.
Humans need no guidance at all
Not quite. The article says: It is unlikely that the one creature charged with moral choice was left without guidance – so revelation is reasonable to expect.
questions.rationale: “It is implausible that the one creature tasked with moral choice should be denied any corresponding guidance.”

questions.q: How does the article explain why even great achievers die feeling unfulfilled?
options: Man’s mind seeks the unlimited and perfect, while his body and this world are limited
Correct. This life is for sowing; the harvest comes later.
Fulfilment is a matter of luck
Not quite. The article says: Man’s mind seeks the unlimited and perfect, while his body and this world are limited.
They were poorly advised
Not quite. The article says: Man’s mind seeks the unlimited and perfect, while his body and this world are limited.
They did not work hard enough
Not quite. The article says: Man’s mind seeks the unlimited and perfect, while his body and this world are limited.
questions.rationale: “Intellectually he is unlimited in capability but physically he is a limited being. This disparity in his inner nature causes the problem.”

questions.article: Love for God Beyond Worldly Attachments
questions.q: What does the article say our feelings of love and attachment for family are meant to teach us?
options: That family should be loved less
Not quite. The article says: How to direct love towards God – they are seeds that reach their fullness only when turned to Him.
That emotions are a weakness
Not quite. The article says: How to direct love towards God – they are seeds that reach their fullness only when turned to Him.
How to direct love towards God – they are seeds that reach their fullness only when turned to Him
Yes. We still serve our families with tenderness.
That loss should make us bitter
Not quite. The article says: How to direct love towards God – they are seeds that reach their fullness only when turned to Him.
questions.rationale: “God placed these feelings within us so we might learn how to direct them toward Him… they attain their fullness only when turned towards God.”

questions.q: Why does the article call the home “a natural training ground”?
options: Rules at home are stricter than outside
Not quite. The article says: Good character practised in the small circle of the family carries into the wider circle of society.
Home is where people rest
Not quite. The article says: Good character practised in the small circle of the family carries into the wider circle of society.
Good character practised in the small circle of the family carries into the wider circle of society
Right. “The best among you are those who are best to their families.”
Children are taught trades at home
Not quite. The article says: Good character practised in the small circle of the family carries into the wider circle of society.
questions.rationale: “If one displays good character within the limited circle of the house, one can exhibit good character within the wider circle of society.”

questions.q: The article describes two kinds of strong will power. Which does it call better?
options: Neither – habits cannot be changed
Not quite. The article says: Reason-based – giving up a habit as a considered decision, not only on an emotional moment.
Emotion-based – acting on a sudden feeling
Not quite. The article says: Reason-based – giving up a habit as a considered decision, not only on an emotional moment.
Reason-based – giving up a habit as a considered decision, not only on an emotional moment
Yes. Thinking a habit through shows what it costs.
Whichever others recommend
Not quite. The article says: Reason-based – giving up a habit as a considered decision, not only on an emotional moment.
questions.rationale: “There are two kinds of strong will power—emotion-based and reason-based… it is better to abandon something on the basis of reason.”

questions.q: According to the Hadith the article explains, to whom should a person look in worldly matters, and to whom in matters of religion?
options: In worldly matters to the rich; in religion to no one
Not quite. The article says: In worldly matters to those who have less; in religion to those who are ahead of him.
In both, to those who have less
Not quite. The article says: In worldly matters to those who have less; in religion to those who are ahead of him.
In worldly matters to those who have less; in religion to those who are ahead of him
Exactly. So gratitude stays alive and he keeps improving.
In both, to those who have more
Not quite. The article says: In worldly matters to those who have less; in religion to those who are ahead of him.
questions.rationale: “In the matters of this world, to look to those who are inferior to him and then be thankful… in matters of religion, to look to those who are superior to him and then to follow them.”

questions.q: A young attendant refused a tip and asked for a prayer for his examination. What did the author see in this?
options: A self-respecting choice of effort over easy money – “the upper hand is better than the lower hand”
Well read. Hard work builds confidence and dignity.
Shyness about taking money
Not quite. The article says: A self-respecting choice of effort over easy money – “the upper hand is better than the lower hand”.
A wish for a larger tip
Not quite. The article says: A self-respecting choice of effort over easy money – “the upper hand is better than the lower hand”.
A rule of the airport
Not quite. The article says: A self-respecting choice of effort over easy money – “the upper hand is better than the lower hand”.
questions.rationale: “It revealed a creative, self-respecting mindset: to choose effort over easy money; to prefer the path of becoming a self-made person rather than relying on a favour.”
